title: Eid al-Fitr
hook: Muslims end Ramadan with prayer, gifts and feasting; on Eid the Prophet tells Abu Bakr to let the girls sing, and zakat al-fitr feeds the poor first
tomorrow: a woman prayed so hard a priest thought she was drunk. then what?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: colors. Prahlad walked out of the fire, and Holi's morning turned bright. Today a feast at the end of a fast.

After a month of fasting, the first daytime meal is a party. Aisha, a wife of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, remembers one Eid in their home. Two girls were singing songs of an old battle. The Prophet lay down and turned his face away. Then Abu Bakr, her father, came in and scolded them: the instruments of Satan, in the Prophet's house? The Prophet turned to him and said: leave them, Abu Bakr. Every people has its Eid, and this is our Eid.
screen: `A MONTH OF FASTING ENDS.` → `TWO GIRLS SINGING.` → `ABU BAKR SCOLDS.` → `THIS IS OUR EID.`

segments.voice: Eid al-Fitr is the festival of breaking the fast, the day after Ramadan ends with the new crescent. It begins with prayer, the whole community together. And before that prayer comes a gift. The Prophet made zakat al-fitr a duty: a measure of food, dates or barley, given for each member of the household, young or old, before people go out to the prayer. His cousin Ibn Abbas reports that he called it a cleansing for the one who fasted, and food for those in need. In Islam, the end of the fast isn't only a private relief. It's a shared joy, and joy belongs to the day, as the singing girls show: this is our Eid. But no one is meant to be left outside it. So the feast begins with food going to those who have little. Muslims greet each other with Eid mubarak, blessed Eid, and the day is generous on purpose: new clothes, sweets, visits to family, gifts for the children. And the order matters. First the gift and the prayer, then the feast.
screen: `THE FESTIVAL OF BREAKING THE FAST.` · `ZAKAT AL-FITR: FOOD BEFORE THE PRAYER.` · `JOY BELONGS TO THE DAY.` · `FIRST THE GIFT, THEN THE FEAST.` · then, large: `EID MUBARAK.`

segments.voice: Think of one person who'd be glad of food this week: a neighbor, a coworker, someone who's had a hard month. Decide what you'll bring them, something simple, and when. If it helps, send them a message now to say it's coming.
Eid al-Fitr: the festival of breaking the fast, begun with prayer and a gift of food so everyone can feast.
Keep this one: eid mubarak. Blessed Eid, with the food given before the feast begins. Until next time.

howItsDone: Muslims pay zakat al-fitr, a measure of staple food or its value for each household member, before the Eid prayer; on the morning of Eid they pray together, greet each other with Eid mubarak, wear new or best clothes, visit family and share sweets.
